title: Implement small-prime GEMM kernels
description:
Implement the selected small-prime GF(p) GEMM improvements per the design at `dev/plans/small_prime_kernel_strategy.md` (Candidate C — AVX2 16-bit-lane SIMD with Barrett reduction).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] GF(7) and GF(31) small-prime GEMM target rows at $n \in \{64, 256, 1024\}^3$ are within 1.5× of fflas-ffpack 2.5.0 or faster, measured on the pinned bench host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, Zen-3, AVX2; no AVX-512).
- [aspirational] GF(251) small-prime GEMM target rows at $n \in \{64, 256, 1024\}^3$ are within 1.5× of fflas-ffpack 2.5.0 or faster on the same pinned host.
  * **Empirical amendment basis (recorded at design time per `CLAUDE.md` § Success-criterion maturity markers):** fflas's GF(251) `n = 256³` cell hits 128 Gop/s via Modular<float> + OpenBLAS sgemm (Candidate D in the design); the 1.5× target is therefore 85.3 Gop/s. The AVX2 16-bit-MAC peak at 5 GHz on the pinned host is 80 Gop/s — reaching 85.3 Gop/s requires 107 % of theoretical peak, which AVX2-only integer SIMD cannot deliver. See `dev/plans/small_prime_kernel_strategy.md` § 6 #2 for the throughput-envelope derivation. The `[aspirational]` marker permits the implementation to ship with the best AVX2-feasible GF(251) number and have it reviewed against the empirical envelope rather than the (unattainable) 1.5× absolute target. The aggregate contract — Candidate C unifies GF(7), GF(31), GF(251) under one dispatch with no per-prime regressions — still holds.
  * **At review time:** `662f7a15` records the measured GF(251) ratio. If the implementation closes within ~1.6×–2× of fflas, the amendment is honored. If it falls below ~50 % of AVX2-MAC peak (= 40 Gop/s, i.e. ratio worse than ~3.2× of fflas), escalate per the same policy with the measured number for re-amendment or scope decision.
- [hard] Correctness is covered by property and reference tests at `WORD_BOUNDARY_LENS = [0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257]` for each new prime, asserting the SIMD path matches the scalar element-wise path bit-exactly. The new tests slot into `crates/gf2-core/src/gfp/simd_ops.rs::tests::generic_simd_matches_scalar_for_proof_suite_primes` per the design § 7 step 1.
- [hard] Mersenne31 and Fp<65537> existing dispatch paths do not regress — `cargo bench -p gf2-core --bench fieldmatrix_gemm -- --filter mersenne` and `--filter fp65537` show throughput delta ≤ 5 % vs. the pre-implementation baseline.
